Mr Serajur Rahman Advocate-on-Record For the Appellants 
Abdur Rahman, Advocate instructed by Mr Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record For the respondents

Mosammat Momina Begum and others……..Appellants
Vs.
Mst. Sahera Khatun and others………Respondents
full_judgment:
We have heard both the sides and examined documents and evidence adduce by the parties. Admittedly, the partition deed in question was executed by the defendants by going to the Sub-Registry Office, Gazipur, obviously with full knowledge that a deed was executed and registered on 7.3.1960 (Exhibit-1). The said deed has never been challenged by the defendants in any suit seeking cancellation of the deed with the allegation of fraud, undue influence, etc. under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act. Where a written instrument is void ab anitio/ab initio, the transaction is nullity, the document does not require to be cancelled and the party can avoid it even as defendants in suit of the present nature brought by others. But in the present case, the defendants being admitted executants of the deed, the same is only avoidable at the option of executing parties. As such it is incumbent upon the defendants to have it cancelled or set aside by filing a suit under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. It is an absurd proposition of the learned Advocate for the appellant to bring amendment in the written statement seeking such cancellation as defendants in this suit. The defendant cannot get decree for such relief in the instituted by their adversaries. Therefore, the submission of the learned Advocate for the Appellants is totally without sub-stance. It is also an admitted fact that the insertion of the plot Nos. 103 and 108 in the disputed partition deed was an advertent mistake. None of the parties or their predecessors had or have any interest in respect of lands involved in those two plots. At the time of hearing before us, the learned Advocate for the appellant side conceded that insertion of those two plots in the deed was a mistake occurred inadvertently. But the defendants want to resist correction of the deed to remove admitted error challenging the validity of the partition deed itself. But in a suit of the present nature, the defendants cannot get any relief by way of the cancellation of the partition deed in question as we have stated above. The plaintiffs, in fact, filed the suit in a declaratory form seeking simple declaration that the two plot numbers in the partition deed were wrongly inserted. Since the suit was for declaration under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act such a simple declaration about the incorrectness of the plot numbers in the deed was not adequate to get proper relief in the matter. Because the deed in question would remain incorrect as before in spite of such declaration. So, correction of the deed in question is the proper relief which ought to have been asked for by the plaintiffs as a consequential relief. However, the plaintiff-respondents got their plaint amended before the appellate court on 04.12.2001 seeking such consequential relief in the form of making correction of the document by the concerned Sub-register. Requisite Court fees have also been paid. In view of such amendment, the defect has already been cured and there is no bar to maintain the suit for simple correction of the document.   In consequence of mistake in writing plot numbers, shares of the partition shown the R.S. Khatian are wrong. So, we do not find any legality in the second declaration allowed by the Court below. It may be mentioned that witnesses of both sides admitted possession of the plaintiffs and defendants in the suit land. Having due regard to the aforesaid facts, circumstances and evidences on record, we find that the plaintiffs are entitled to get the impugned partition deed corrected and also get declaration as given by the court below. There is no ground to disagree with the learned trial court in this respect. However, in view of subsequent amendment in the plaint on 04.12.2001, we are inclined to modify the ordering portion of the judgment in an appropriate manner." 

 15. Admittedly, the defendants i.e. the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 contested the said suit. Therefore, they had full knowledge about the suit property as the boundary of the suit property was mentioned clearly in the said deed with khatian numbers, etc. Only there was some inadvertent mistake in writing down the plot numbers i.e. C.S. Plot Nos. 103 and 108 were written in place of C.S. Plot Nos. 1003 and 1008. Therefore, when the plaintiffs allegedly came to know about the deed of partition in the said suit i.e. in the year 1989, they had definite knowledge about the deed of partition but they have not filed the suit for cancellation of the said deed or any declaration that the impugned deed of partition is fraudulent, illegal, etc. Rather, they had prayed for cancellation of said deed as defendants by way of amendment of the written statement. Therefore, it is evident that the cause of action for the suit arose in the year 1989 but the plaintiffs have filed Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 for declaration that the deed of partition is forged, fraudulent collusive, not acted upon, etc. in the year 2002 i.e. more than 12 years after. Thus, in view of the provision of Article 91 of the Limitation Act, 1908 the suit having not filed within a period of three years from the date of knowledge is hopelessly barred by limitation.
